title: Man. Post. Cap. III: Laudo fons/radix — nature law not judge sentence; before-fall decree
pass_a_gloss: I also praise these your words: Just as an infected fountain also infects the streams, and as a root produces shoots according to its own species—bad ones, namely, if it is bad—IN EXACTLY THE SAME WAY the first man, corrupted and a sinner, begot and brought forth corrupted and sinful sons. I subsume: but an infected fountain infects streams and a bad root brings forth bad shoots only by that law of Nature by which each thing begets its like. Why then do you not hold the same of the first man, if corrupted he begot us corrupted in exactly the same way? If that law of nature, constituted and sanctioned before the sin, suffices for the propagation of original sin, why do you impute it to the justice of God, to the sentence of God the judge—not without my great scandal, who complain that great injury is done to God's justice? And the very name of propagation could have warned you of this: for propagation is a work of nature, which follows its laws in it, God as nature's author and conserver conserving and establishing those laws by His concurrence; for they hang on a decree which, in the order of nature, seems to me to have preceded the decree permitting the fall. And so they could not, nor ought they, be rescinded by a later decree.
pass_b_english: I also praise these words of yours: just as a polluted spring pollutes its streams, and as a root puts out shoots after its own kind—bad shoots if the root is bad—IN EXACTLY THE SAME WAY the first man, corrupted and a sinner, begot and brought forth corrupted, sinful children.

I take that up. A polluted spring infects its streams, and a bad root yields bad shoots, only by nature's law that each thing begets its like. Why not say the same of the first man, if corrupted he begot us corrupted in exactly that way? If that natural law, already set and sanctioned before the sin, is enough to propagate original sin, why charge it to God's justice and to the sentence of God the Judge—to my great scandal, who complain that God's justice is deeply wronged? The very word "propagation" could have warned you: propagation is nature's work, following nature's laws, while God, as nature's author and conserver, keeps those laws in force by His concurrence. They hang on a decree that, in nature's order, seems to me to have come before the decree permitting the fall. A later decree neither could nor should undo them.
source_text: Laudo etiam haec tua verba, Quemadmodum fons infectus rivos etiam inficit, & sicut radix producit surculos secundum speciem suam, malos scilicet, si mala est, EODEM PRORSUS MODO primus homo corruptus & peccator genuit & protulit filios corruptos & peccatores. Subsumo, atqui fons infectus inficit rivos & radix mala profert malos surculos ea tantummodo lege Naturae, qua sibi quodque simile gignit. Cur igitur non idem statuis de primo homine, si nos eodem prorsus modo corruptus corruptos genuit? Si lex ista naturae sufficit ad peccati originalis propagationem ante peccatum constituta & sancita, quid est quamobrem eam dei justitiae, dei judicis sententiae imputes non sine magno meo scandalo, qui sic magnam Dei justitiae fieri injuriam queror? atque hujus te rei ipsum propagationis nomen admonere potuit: est enim propagatio opus naturae, quae suas in ea leges sequitur, Deo, ut est naturae author & conservator, leges illas suo concursu conservante & constabiliente, pendent enim ex decreto, quod ordine naturae decretum de lapsu permittendo mihi videtur antecessisse. Itaque posteriore decreto rescindi nec potuerunt, nec debuerunt.

choices.choice: Keep nature-law propagation; refuse judge-sentence reading
